references.text: When Jesus called the disciples, they left everything and followed him. Peter refers to this moment when he says "we have left everything and followed you" ([ref:Matt 4:20-22|Matthew 4:20-22]).
The parallel passage in Matthew where Peter says exactly the same thing: "See, we have left everything and followed you" ([ref:Matt 19:27|Matthew 19:27]).
The parallel passage in Mark where Peter says: "See, we have left everything and followed you" ([ref:Mark 10:28|Mark 10:28]).
When Peter was called by Jesus, he left everything and followed him – this is the background for his statement here ([ref:Luk 5:11|Luke 5:11]).
Levi (Matthew) also left everything and followed Jesus, just as Peter describes here that the disciples have done ([ref:Luk 5:28|Luke 5:28]).
Jesus' teaching that whoever does not give up all they own cannot be his disciple – Peter's statement shows that the disciples have met this requirement ([ref:Luk 14:33|Luke 14:33]).
Paul expresses the same principle – counting everything as loss to gain Christ – which Peter here illustrates by having left everything to follow Jesus ([ref:Fil 3:7-8|Philippians 3:7-8]).
The tribe of Levi left family and property for the Lord's sake, an example of the sacrifice the disciples made by leaving everything to follow Jesus ([ref:5 Mos 33:9|Deuteronomy 33:9]).
